seoTitle: How to Connect a GoDaddy Domain to Webflow (Quick Connect or Manual DNS)
metaDescription: Point a GoDaddy domain at Webflow using the one-click Quick Connect option or manual DNS records, without breaking the email inbox on the same domain.
intro:
Pointing a domain you bought on GoDaddy at a Webflow site comes down to telling Webflow which domain to expect and making sure DNS routes traffic there. Webflow added a Quick Connect option built specifically for GoDaddy, which handles the DNS side through an authorization flow, so most people no longer need to copy records by hand.

This guide covers Quick Connect first, then the manual DNS path for anyone whose domain isn't on GoDaddy's default nameservers, plus the email-safety check that matters most either way.
prerequisites: A domain registered with GoDaddy that you already own
A Webflow site on a paid Site plan, since custom domain connections require one
costNote: Custom domain connections need a paid Webflow Site plan. Webflow's documentation states this applies to every site you connect a domain to, with no exception on the free starter tier.

steps.heading: Open the domain settings in Webflow
steps.body: In the Designer, click Publish in the top right to open the destination picker, or go to Site settings, then Publishing. Under Production you'll see an Add a custom domain link once no custom domain is attached. Clicking it offers two paths: Quick connect domain, which automates the DNS side for supported providers, and Manually connect domain, for anyone who'd rather add the records themselves.

image.caption: Webflow's Choose publish destination panel, with the Staging subdomain checked and an "Add a custom domain" link under Production.

steps.heading: Try Quick Connect first
steps.body:
Quick Connect uses a service called Entri to detect your DNS provider and configure everything automatically. Choose GoDaddy from the provider list, sign in with your GoDaddy credentials, and authorize Entri to manage the domain's DNS. Webflow then adds the A and CNAME records for both the root domain and the www subdomain, plus the TXT verification record it needs.

This only works if the domain is still on GoDaddy's default nameservers, ns01.domaincontrol.com and ns02.domaincontrol.com. If you've pointed it elsewhere, skip to the manual method below.

steps.heading: Get your DNS values for a manual connection
steps.body: If Quick Connect isn't offered, or you'd rather not authorize a third party to touch DNS directly, choose Manually connect domain and type in the domain exactly as you own it, with no https:// prefix. Webflow generates the records your DNS needs: an A record for the root domain, a CNAME for www, and a TXT record used only to verify you control the domain. Copy these values somewhere you can paste from before switching to GoDaddy.

steps.heading: Log into GoDaddy and open DNS management
steps.body: From your GoDaddy account dashboard, go to the Domain section for the site you're connecting. This is the same account hub where you manage renewals, billing, and any hosting products tied to the domain, so confirm you're editing DNS on the correct domain if you manage more than one. A wrong edit here affects live traffic immediately, not after a review step.

image.caption: The GoDaddy account dashboard, with Domain and Website listed in the left sidebar alongside billing and account settings.

steps.heading: Add the A, CNAME and TXT records
steps.body:
In GoDaddy's DNS records editor, set the A record on host @ to 198.202.211.1, add a CNAME record on host www pointing to cdn.webflow.com, and add the TXT record on host _webflow with the one-time-verification value exactly as Webflow displayed it. A single mismatched character fails verification.

Before saving anything, scroll through the existing record list and confirm your MX records are untouched. Those route your email, and they live in the same table as the records you're about to change, which is exactly how people accidentally break their inbox during a domain move.

steps.heading: Set your default domain in Webflow
steps.body: Back in Webflow's domain settings, decide whether the root domain or the www version should be the canonical one that the other redirects to. Search engines treat these as separate URLs unless you pick one, so leaving both live without a redirect can quietly split your SEO signals. Most sites default to the root domain, but either choice works as long as it's consistent.

steps.heading: Check propagation and publish
steps.body: DNS changes don't take effect instantly. Propagation can run from a few minutes up to 48 hours depending on your previous records' TTL settings. Use any DNS checker to confirm the new records are visible, then return to the publish panel, check your new domain alongside staging, and click Publish. SSL provisions automatically once Webflow confirms the domain is correctly pointed, so an inactive certificate is usually a sign DNS hasn't fully propagated, not a Webflow-side problem.

tables.title: Quick Connect vs. manual DNS
rows: Domain still on GoDaddy's default nameservers; paid Webflow Site plan
Signs in to GoDaddy via Entri and adds the A, CNAME and TXT records automatically, for both root and www
Access to GoDaddy's DNS records editor; paid Webflow Site plan
You copy the exact A, CNAME and TXT values Webflow generates into GoDaddy yourself

troubleshooting.problem: Quick Connect isn't offered as an option
troubleshooting.cause: The domain isn't using GoDaddy's default nameservers, ns01.domaincontrol.com and ns02.domaincontrol.com, which Quick Connect needs to detect GoDaddy as the provider.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the manual DNS method instead, or point the domain back at GoDaddy's default nameservers first if you'd rather use Quick Connect.

troubleshooting.cause: The value was copied with an extra space or a truncated character, or it was added under the wrong host.
troubleshooting.fix: Recopy the one-time-verification value from Webflow exactly, and confirm it's on the host _webflow, not the root domain.

troubleshooting.problem: Email stops working after the domain change
troubleshooting.cause: An MX record was edited or deleted while adding the A, CNAME and TXT records, since they live in the same DNS table.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the current MX records against what your email provider expects and restore any that changed.

troubleshooting.cause: SSL provisions only after Webflow confirms DNS has fully propagated, which can take up to 48 hours.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait and recheck the domain status in Webflow's publish panel instead of assuming something failed.

faq.question: What's the difference between Quick Connect and manual DNS?
faq.answer: Quick Connect signs in to GoDaddy through an authorization service called Entri and adds the required records for you; it only works if the domain is still on GoDaddy's default nameservers. Manual DNS means copying the A, CNAME and TXT values Webflow gives you into GoDaddy's DNS editor yourself, and it works regardless of nameservers.

faq.question: Will connecting my domain break my existing email?
faq.answer: It shouldn't, as long as your MX records are left untouched while you add the records for Webflow. Check the full record list in GoDaddy before saving any changes, or before authorizing Quick Connect.

faq.question: Do I need both an A record and a CNAME record?
faq.answer: Yes, for a manual connection: the A record on host @ points the root domain to 198.202.211.1, and the CNAME on host www points to cdn.webflow.com. Quick Connect adds both automatically.

faq.question: How long does it take for the domain to go live?
faq.answer: DNS propagation can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours depending on your provider and the TTL on your existing records, so don't assume something's broken if it's not instant.

faq.question: Why isn't my SSL certificate showing as active?
faq.answer: SSL provisioning depends on DNS fully propagating first, so give it time and recheck the domain status in Webflow's publish panel before assuming something is wrong.
